chunks: Muḥammad ibn Qays narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled concerning a group who slaughtered a camel and ate it. They were examined as to which of them had slaughtered it, and they testified against themselves that they had all slaughtered it together, without singling out one person over another. So he ruled that their right hands be cut off.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام, Commander of the Faithful
key_terms.تُقْطَعَ أَيْمَانُهُمْ: their right hands are to be cut off as the legal punishment
key_terms.فَشَهِدُوا عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ: they testified against themselves by self-confession
key_terms.قَضَى: ruled or issued a judicial judgment
key_terms.نَحَرُوا: they slaughtered by cutting the throat area of the animal

ai.seo_question: How did Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام rule when several people jointly confessed to slaughtering and eating a stolen camel?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a judicial ruling of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام in a case involving collective admission to an act of theft and slaughter. It highlights legal accountability when a group jointly confesses to the act without distinguishing one offender from another, and it reflects the implementation of the hadd punishment in such a case.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5108 - Muhammad ibn Qays narrated from Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) who said:

"Commander of the Faithful (as) ruled in the case of a group of people who slaughtered a camel and ate it. They were investigated to determine who among them had slaughtered it, and they all testified against themselves that they had collectively slaughtered it without specifying any individual over another. So, Imam (as) ruled that their right hands be cut off."
